bibl.title: Eighteen-Month-Old Infants Show Increased Helping Following Priming with Affiliation

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: We show that the mere hint of affiliation dramatically increases prosocial behavior in infants.

span.label: social priming of prosocial helping in infants
span.quote: In the study described here, we tested whether connections between affiliation to the group and prosocial behaviors are so fundamental that they are seen even in infants.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: In the current study, we primed 18-month-old infants with photographs evoking affiliation (two small dolls standing next to each other in the background of photographs of other objects) and measured the influence of the primes on infants’ tendency to be helpful.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The affiliation photographs activate a general prosocial orientation, which is then expressed in an unrelated helping act, rather than being copied from what was depicted
span.quote: Infants did not directly reproduce the situations depicted in the photographs; instead, the photographs triggered a general prosocial orientation that manifested itself in increased helping.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An implicit, non-conscious link between affiliation to the group and helping is engaged by the prime
span.quote: Thus, infants made the subconscious connection between affiliation and helping behavior.

span.label: Baseline helping rates were lower than in an earlier helping study, leaving open the alternative reading that the affiliation condition is the true baseline and the other three conditions suppressed helping.
span.quote: This raises the possibility that our together condition represents a true baseline and the other three conditions depressed helping below baseline levels.

span.label: Procedural choices (a single helping opportunity, and a different experimenter interacting with the infant beforehand) probably lowered helping in every condition, so rates are not comparable across studies.
span.quote: In contrast, infants in our study were presented with only one chance to help and had been interacting with a different experimenter immediately before the test phase, which likely reduced their tendency to help across all four conditions.

span.label: attentiveness and mood were measured and compared across conditions
span.note: eliminates: that infants in the together condition simply paid more attention or were in a better mood, and helped more for that reason rather than because of the affiliation prime
span.quote: Thus, infants’ increased helping in the together condition cannot be explained by differences in attentiveness or mood.

span.label: an INDIVIDUALITY prime condition run alongside the affiliation prime and the baseline
span.note: eliminates: that any social prime raises helping - the individuality prime shares the format and the social content and should produce the effect if format is what matters
span.quote: By comparing the results of the together condition to the baseline control condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliation primes that increased helping behavior rather than the individuality primes that decreased it.

span.label: affiliation
span.quote: In the current study, we primed 18-month-old infants with photographs evoking affiliation (two small dolls standing next to each other in the background of photographs of other objects) and measured the influence of the primes on infants’ tendency to be helpful.

span.label: individuality
span.quote: Eighteen-month-old infants helped a person in need more often, and more spontaneously, when primed with photographs evoking affiliation than when primed with photographs evoking individuality.

span.label: helping
span.quote: The connections between affiliation to the group and prosocial behavior are thus so fundamental that, even in infancy, a mere hint of affiliation is sufficient to increase helping.

span.label: helping behavior
span.quote: By comparing the results of the together condition to the baseline control condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliation primes that increased helping behavior rather than the individuality primes that decreased it.

span.label: prosocial behavior
span.quote: The connections between affiliation to the group and prosocial behavior are thus so fundamental that, even in infancy, a mere hint of affiliation is sufficient to increase helping.

span.label: prosocial orientation
span.quote: Infants did not directly reproduce the situations depicted in the photographs; instead, the photographs triggered a general prosocial orientation that manifested itself in increased helping.

span.label: affiliative stance
span.quote: Moreover, by comparing the results of the together condition to the back-to-back condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliative stance depicted in the photographs, rather than the mere presence of two dolls, that increased helping.

span.label: back-to-back
span.quote: Finally, to determine which aspects of the affiliation primes increase helpfulness, we compared the together condition to a condition in which there were also two dolls, but this time standing in a nonaffiliative relation to each other: back-to-back.

span.label: baseline
span.quote: In the baseline condition, each photograph contained a unique configuration of four colored blocks.

span.label: mood
span.quote: Thus, infants’ increased helping in the together condition cannot be explained by differences in attentiveness or mood.

span.label: prime - a BACKGROUND element of a photograph whose foreground is an ordinary household object, and the assistant naming the photograph aloud never refers to it. The construct is delivered by what is deliberately not mentioned
span.quote: For each photograph, the assistant named the foreground object and then commented on its color and finally its function, completely ignoring the prime.

span.label: spontaneous helping - the main dependent measure, and it is defined by a CLOCK rather than by a judgement: within the first 10 s, before the experimenter has spoken to the infant or reached for the sticks herself
span.quote: The main dependent measure was whether infants helped the experimenter spontaneously, that is, whether they picked up at least one stick and offered it to her within the first 10 s of the test phase (before she spoke to the infants or reached for the sticks herself).

span.label: affiliation - as delivered here, an arrangement of two dolls in the background of a photograph, not a word list or a scenario. The whole construct rests on which way two small wooden figures are turned
span.quote: In the current study, we primed 18-month-old infants with photographs evoking affiliation (two small dolls standing next to each other in the background of photographs of other objects) and measured the influence of the primes on infants’ tendency to be helpful.

span.label: the back-to-back condition - the question it exists to answer, in the authors' own words: whether the effect belongs to the DOLLS or to their RELATION
span.quote: This condition was designed to determine whether it is the mere presence of two dolls or their affiliative interaction that increases helpfulness.

span.label: baseline - a condition included not to test the hypothesis but to DISAMBIGUATE THE DIRECTION of the effect: did the affiliation primes raise helping, or the individuality primes lower it
span.quote: Second, to see whether the affiliation primes increase helping (or whether the individual primes decrease it), we included a measure of infants’ baseline tendency to help

span.label: builds-on → Warneken & Tomasello (2006)
span.quote: We know from previous studies that, if an adult is unable to reach an object he wants, 18-month-old infants will often pick up the object themselves and offer it to the adult (Warneken & Tomasello, 2006).

span.label: affiliation —causes→ helping behavior
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95 — THE DIRECTION IS READ OFF A NAMED COMPARISON, not from the two-group result: the non-social baseline is what distinguishes `affiliation raised helping` from `individuality lowered it`, and the authors say which in the same sentence.
span.quote: By comparing the results of the together condition to the baseline control condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliation primes that increased helping behavior rather than the individuality primes that decreased it.

span.label: individuality —causes→ helping behavior
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.1 — the record marks this weak — The negative half of the same sentence, kept as its own edge because it is the half a reader would otherwise have to assume. Shares its span with the edge above, declared.
span.quote: By comparing the results of the together condition to the baseline control condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliation primes that increased helping behavior rather than the individuality primes that decreased it.

span.label: affiliative stance —causes→ helping
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The back-to-back control holds the number of dolls and the visible proportion of their faces constant, so this edge is about WHICH FEATURE of the prime carries the effect.
span.quote: Moreover, by comparing the results of the together condition to the back-to-back condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliative stance depicted in the photographs, rather than the mere presence of two dolls, that increased helping.

span.label: prosocial orientation —causes→ helping
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — SHARED SPAN, DECLARED: also stands under mechanisms[0]. The sentence is the paper's argument against imitation - the primes depict no helping at all - and it is the only place the intervening state is named.
span.quote: Infants did not directly reproduce the situations depicted in the photographs; instead, the photographs triggered a general prosocial orientation that manifested itself in increased helping.

span.label: affiliation —causes→ prosocial orientation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — The theoretical premise, and weighted as one: the sentence says `we may expect`, so this is the expectation the study was designed around rather than something it establishes.
span.quote: Thus, we may expect there to be direct connections between a sense of affiliation to the group and the tendency to adopt a prosocial orientation

span.label: mood —causes→ helping
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.05 — the record marks this weak — A RULED-OUT CONFOUND IS EDGE-SHAPED. Mood was rated by parents and looking time was coded for a third of the infants; neither differed across conditions. Recorded so a later reader does not assume the check was never run.
span.quote: Thus, infants’ increased helping in the together condition cannot be explained by differences in attentiveness or mood.

span.label: chi-squared test
span.quote: Infants were significantly more likely to spontaneously help the experimenter in the together condition than in the pooled control conditions, w2(1, N 5 60) 5 8.57, two-tailed p 5 .003, prep 5 .97, j 5 .38.

span.label: ANOVA (F-test)
span.quote: There were no significant differences between conditions, F(3, 16) 5 1.58, p 5 .23, prep 5 .70.

span.label: Cohen's kappa (interrater reliability)
span.quote: Agreement was perfect for both measures (Cohen’s k 5 1.00).

span.label: p-rep (probability of replication)
span.quote: Infants were significantly more likely to spontaneously help the experimenter in the together condition than in the pooled control conditions, w2(1, N 5 60) 5 8.57, two-tailed p 5 .003, prep 5 .97, j 5 .38.

span.label: mean
span.quote: The average number of seconds spent looking at the photographs was 102.2 in the together condition, 92.8 in the alone condition, 89.6 in the baseline condition, and 101.4 in the back-to-back condition.

span.label: Eighteen-month-old infants who saw photographs with an affiliation prime (two dolls facing each other) helped an adult in need more often and more spontaneously than infants primed with individuality (a single doll).
span.quote: Eighteen-month-old infants helped a person in need more often, and more spontaneously, when primed with photographs evoking affiliation than when primed with photographs evoking individuality.

span.label: Spontaneous helping was three times as frequent after the affiliation prime as in each of the alone, baseline and back-to-back control conditions.
span.quote: Three times as many infants helped spontaneously in the together condition as in each of the other three conditions.

span.label: Comparison with the non-social baseline shows the direction of the effect: the affiliation prime raised helping rather than the individuality prime lowering it.
span.quote: By comparing the results of the together condition to the baseline control condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliation primes that increased helping behavior rather than the individuality primes that decreased it.

span.label: What drove the increase was the affiliative stance of the two dolls toward each other, not the mere presence of two dolls, since the back-to-back condition contained the same two dolls but did not raise helping.
span.quote: Moreover, by comparing the results of the together condition to the back-to-back condition, we can conclude that it was the affiliative stance depicted in the photographs, rather than the mere presence of two dolls, that increased helping.

span.label: Neither how long infants looked at the photographs nor their rated mood differed across the four conditions, so attentiveness and mood cannot account for the helping difference.
span.quote: Thus, infants’ increased helping in the together condition cannot be explained by differences in attentiveness or mood.

span.label: Helping itself was never depicted in the primes - the dolls only stood beside one another - so the effect is not imitation of a modelled action.
span.quote: It is important to note that helpfulness itself was not primed: The dolls simply stood next to one another.

span.label: spontaneous helping (main dependent measure)
span.quote: The main dependent measure was whether infants helped the experimenter spontaneously, that is, whether they picked up at least one stick and offered it to her within the first 10 s of the test phase (before she spoke to the infants or reached for the sticks herself).

span.label: general measure of helping
span.quote: In addition, a more general measure of helping was scored if infants picked up at least one stick and offered it to the experimenter at any point during the test phase (i.e., including after she asked for help).

span.label: prosocial behavior
span.quote: Most notably, it has created a tendency for us to engage in behaviors that benefit our group members, that is, prosocial behaviors such as helping and sharing (Gintis, Bowles, Boyd, & Fehr, 2003). Yet, prosocial behavior

span.label: together (affiliation) prime condition
span.quote: appeared in the background. In the together condition, each prime consisted of two small wooden dolls facing each other in close proximity. In the alone condition,

span.label: back-to-back condition (its diagnostic purpose)
span.quote: This condition was designed to determine whether it is the mere presence of two dolls or their affiliative interaction that increases helpfulness.

span.label: prime type (together / alone / baseline / back-to-back photographs)
span.term: prime type (together / alone / baseline / back-to-back photographs)
span.quote: In the current study, we primed 18-month-old infants with photographs evoking affiliation (two small dolls standing next to each other in the background of photographs of other objects) and measured the influence of the primes on infants’ tendency to be helpful.

span.label: spontaneous helping within the first 10 s
span.term: spontaneous helping within the first 10 s
span.quote: The main dependent measure was whether infants helped the experimenter spontaneously, that is, whether they picked up at least one stick and offered it to her within the first 10 s of the test phase (before she spoke to the infants or reached for the sticks herself).

span.label: infants' mood (parent-rated)
span.quote: There were also no significant differences in infants’ mood across the four conditions, F(3, 56) 5 0.155, p 5 .93, prep 5 .15.

span.label: proportion of the dolls' faces visible (low-level social stimulus content)
span.term: proportion of the dolls' faces visible (low-level social stimulus content)
span.quote: Furthermore, the angle at which the dolls were placed meant that infants in these two conditions were exposed to exactly the same proportion of the dolls’ faces (that is, they saw the same number of eyes, and the same proportion of the dolls’ smiles), thus controlling for possible effects of lower-level social stimuli on helping behavior.

span.label: attention to the primes (seconds spent looking at the photographs)
span.term: attention to the primes (seconds spent looking at the photographs)
span.quote: To ascertain whether infants paid equal attention to the presentation of the primes in each condition, we randomly selected a third of the infants from each condition and coded the number of seconds they spent looking at the photographs.

span.label: sixty — number of 18-month-old infants in the study
span.quote: Participants were sixty 18-month-old infants (age range 5 18 months 0 days to 18 months 29 days; 27 boys, 33 girls) recruited from a database of parents who had volunteered to participate in child development studies.

span.label: Fifteen — infants per condition (four conditions)
span.quote: Fifteen infants participated in each condition.

span.label: 7 — additional infants tested but excluded from analysis, for parental interference, crying, experimenter error and refusal to look
span.quote: An additional 7 infants were tested but excluded from analyses for parental interference (n 5 3), crying during the test (n 5 2), experimenter error (n 5 1), and refusal to observe some of the photographs (n 5 1).

span.label: Three times — ratio of infants helping spontaneously in the together condition to each control condition
span.quote: Three times as many infants helped spontaneously in the together condition as in each of the other three conditions.

span.label: w2(1, N 5 60) 5 8.57, two-tailed p 5 .003 — chi-square test of spontaneous helping, together versus pooled controls
span.quote: Infants were significantly more likely to spontaneously help the experimenter in the together condition than in the pooled control conditions, w2(1, N 5 60) 5 8.57, two-tailed p 5 .003, prep 5 .97, j 5 .38.

span.label: w2(1, N 5 60) 5 6.43, two-tailed p 5 .011 — chi-square test of overall helping (including after prompting), together versus pooled controls
span.quote: Again, infants were significantly more likely to help in the together condition than in the pooled control conditions, w2(1, N 5 60) 5 6.43, two-tailed p 5 .011, prep 5 .95, j 5 .33.

span.label: Cohen’s k 5 1.00 — interrater agreement on both helping measures for the 20% of tapes double-coded
span.quote: Agreement was perfect for both measures (Cohen’s k 5 1.00).

span.label: 102.2 / 92.8 / 89.6 / 101.4 — mean seconds spent looking at the photographs in the together, alone, baseline and back-to-back conditions
span.quote: The average number of seconds spent looking at the photographs was 102.2 in the together condition, 92.8 in the alone condition, 89.6 in the baseline condition, and 101.4 in the back-to-back condition.
